key_insight: Engineering Hilbert-space geometry can align low-energy states with target optimization solutions and enable diabatic annealing through target-compatible excited states.
engineering_relevance: This framework could guide neutral-atom Rydberg-array designs and annealing protocols by identifying geometry-induced optimization bottlenecks.
method: Study blockaded-chain models whose boundary terms encode a target maximum independent set problem.
Model bulk-induced auxiliary problems using independent sets of cliques and physically derived clique weights.
Test a diabatic strategy that exploits target-compatible excited states on diamond-chain graphs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports approximate spectral modeling and tests on diamond-chain graphs, but provides no numerical performance gains or hardware benchmarks.
watch_item: Benefits depend on consistency between target and auxiliary problems; applicability beyond the studied graph family remains uncertain.
paper_title: Quantum adiabatic and diabatic optimization: A Hilbert space engineering strategy with Rydberg arrays
